3. Risks of write-back to WeChat and chat record editing
1. Write-back to WeChat modifies WeChat's own database. It may cause WeChat to fail to start or crash, chat records to be lost or scrambled, your account to be restricted, frozen or banned by WeChat, and a mismatch with WeChat's cloud data.
2. Backup and restore are best-effort protection only and are not guaranteed to work in every case. A backup may take a lot of storage, and may fail because of changes in the device, system or WeChat.

Reading or writing WeChat data requires root access. Rooting may void the warranty, make the system unstable, break banking and payment apps, weaken security protections and expose data to other apps. Whether to root, and by which method, is your decision and your risk.

Using such tools may violate WeChat's terms of service, and WeChat may restrict or terminate your account because of it. WeChat and its data formats may change at any time, and the developer has no duty to follow.

2. Reading, copying, exporting or sharing other people's chat records without authorization may infringe their rights and carry legal liability. The developer is not liable for how you use WeDeep.
3. You must protect exported files and data from access by unauthorized people.

7. AI analysis
1. The AI is provided by a third-party model provider you configure yourself. The developer does not control, and is not responsible for, its models, service, prices, availability or data handling.
2. The chat content you select is sent to that provider after you confirm, and may be stored, logged or used by it. Send only what you are entitled to send, and read the provider's terms and privacy policy yourself.
3. AI output may be wrong, invented, incomplete or biased. It is not legal, medical, financial, psychological or any other professional advice, and must not be the basis of decisions or evidence. Verify it yourself.
4. You keep the provider key. Leaks, misuse or charges arising from the key are yours to bear.

4. A suspension does not delete your local data. Keep your own backups and exports of important data.

Important
Please read this agreement in full before using WeDeep, especially the sections on network use, remote disabling of features, chat record editing and write-back, and limitation of liability. By tapping Agree, continuing to use or reopening WeDeep, you confirm that you have read, understood and accepted this agreement and the Disclaimer in full. If you do not agree with any part of them, stop using WeDeep and uninstall it immediately.

1. Nature and purpose of the software
1. WeDeep is a tool, provided by an individual developer, for viewing, searching, exporting and optionally editing copies of WeChat chat records on your own device.
2. WeDeep is not an official WeChat product and has no affiliation, partnership or authorization with Tencent or WeChat. Names and marks such as WeChat belong to their owners and are used here only to describe compatibility.
3. WeDeep is intended for legitimate uses such as backing up, organizing and reading your own chat records. It does not provide or encourage any use that infringes the rights of others.

2. Eligibility
1. You must have full civil capacity. Minors must use WeDeep together with, and with the consent of, a guardian.
2. You must make sure that the law where you live permits you to use this software and the techniques it involves. If it does not, do not use it.
3. You warrant that all accounts, data and files you give to WeDeep belong to you, or that you hold lawful, explicit and still valid authorization to use them.

3. Lawful use and prohibited conduct
You must not use WeDeep for any of the following. You alone are responsible if you do:
1. reading, importing, decrypting, exporting, editing or distributing another person's chat records, contacts or other personal information without that person's explicit authorization or a legal basis;
2. stealing accounts, bypassing authentication, monitoring or eavesdropping on others, or helping others do so;
3. forging or altering chat records and using them for fraud, extortion, defamation, falsification, false evidence, evading liability or any other unlawful purpose;
4. infringing the privacy, reputation, copyright or other lawful rights of others;
5. decompiling, cracking, interfering with or attacking the WeDeep service, or circumventing remote disabling, statistics or consent checks;
6. using WeDeep or its output in any activity that violates law, public order or the terms of a third-party service.
Where such conduct is found or suspected, the developer may, within what the law allows, restrict the affected versions through the remote disabling function and cooperate with the authorities where the law requires.

4. Data sources and your authorization
1. WeDeep works on data you supply yourself: either WeChat's local data read on a device where you have granted root access, or a data file you packaged and imported.
2. You understand and confirm that reading or decrypting WeChat databases may violate WeChat's terms of service. Any account restriction, ban or other consequence is yours alone.
3. Whether to grant root access, choose files, use AI analysis or send statistics is your decision, and you may refuse or withdraw at any time.

5. Data handling and local storage
1. Imported copies, decrypted databases, caches and exported files are stored on your device. Content in the app's private storage can be deleted at any time from the account page or the system settings.
2. WeDeep does not upload chat records, contacts, account information, decryption keys or any file to the WeDeep service.
3. You are responsible for the security of your device. If the device is rooted, infected with malware, lost or used by someone else, the data stored on it may be obtained by others. The developer cannot control this and is not liable for it.
4. You must keep decrypted data, exported files and AI provider keys safe.

6. Chat record editing and write-back to WeChat
1. Chat record editing lets you add, change or delete messages on a copy kept inside WeDeep, and produce install files or screenshots. This affects only the copy, not WeChat.
2. Write-back to WeChat writes your edits into WeChat's own database on a rooted device. While it runs, the WeChat process is paused or ended, and a backup of the original database is kept in WeChat's directory before anything is written. You can restore it from WeDeep.
3. This function carries inherent risks, including WeChat data corruption or failure to start, loss of chat records, restriction or ban of your account by WeChat, and changed behavior after WeChat updates. Backup and restore are not guaranteed to succeed in every case. Before use you must fully back up your WeChat data and device yourself, and you bear all consequences.
4. Edited content is not a genuine chat record, has no evidentiary value and must not be presented as genuine. You must not use it to defraud or deceive anyone, to fabricate or to give false evidence.

7. Exported files
Exported JSON, HTML, attachments and screenshots are saved where you choose, and may contain personal information, images, voice messages and files of you and others. After export, you alone are responsible for keeping, transferring, sharing and destroying the files. Your use of exported content must comply with the law and respect the lawful rights of the people involved.

8. Network use: service status and notices
1. The release build connects to the WeDeep service at launch, when the app returns to the foreground and then periodically (every 60 minutes by default, within 10 to 1440 minutes, adjustable by the service). It reads feature disabling rules, notice text, the latest version number and the check interval.
2. The request carries no device identifier, account information or chat content, and every user receives the same content. The service runs on Cloudflare, which can see your IP address and the time of access, but the service does not store IP addresses.
3. This check is a condition of using WeDeep and cannot be switched off on its own. If you do not accept it, do not use WeDeep.
4. When the service cannot be reached, WeDeep is not blocked for that reason, but it keeps applying the rules last received.

9. Network use: remote disabling of features
1. To reduce legal, security and technical risk, the developer may at any time suspend certain features (accounts and decryption, chat browsing, export, chat record editing, write-back to WeChat, AI analysis) or the whole app through the WeDeep service, limited to certain versions and periods.
2. While a feature is suspended, its entry points are unavailable, or WeDeep shows only an explanation. Reasons include, without limitation: a serious defect, data risk caused by a WeChat update, legal or regulatory requirements, a rights holder's claim, and risk of abuse.
3. The last status received is kept on the device and stays in force offline until the service lifts it or its end time passes.
4. Suspension does not delete, modify or upload your local data. You can still clear this app's data in the system settings. Files you already exported are not affected.
5. The developer makes no commitment on how long a suspension lasts and owes you no compensation for it. Keep your own backups of important data.

10. Network use: usage statistics
1. Off by default. Statistics are sent only after you agree when asked, at most once a day, and you can turn them off at any time in Settings > Privacy.
2. The content is limited to: a randomly generated statistics ID, the WeDeep version, Android version, processor architecture, interface language, and how many times each feature was opened (launch, accounts, chat, export, chat record editing, AI analysis).
3. It contains no chat content, contacts, accounts, device serial numbers or IP addresses. The service infers an approximate country and province from the network source. Details are deleted after 90 days.
4. In Settings > Privacy you can see the full content of the next report or reset the statistics ID. After a reset, earlier reports can no longer be linked to you.

11. Network use: update check
When automatic update checking is on, or when you tap Check for updates, WeDeep reads the latest version number, release notes and download address. After you tap update, the system browser opens the download address; WeDeep itself neither downloads nor installs any program. Obtain installation packages only from trusted sources and check that the signature matches.

12. Network use: AI analysis and third-party services
1. AI analysis uses a model provider you configure yourself. WeDeep neither provides nor proxies any model service.
2. When you fetch the model list, query the balance or test the connection on the configuration page, WeDeep connects to that provider with the key you entered. When you run an analysis, the chat content you selected is sent to that provider after you confirm.
3. This content does not pass through the WeDeep service. Once sent, it is handled under the provider's policies, and may be stored, logged or used for other purposes. The developer cannot control this and is not responsible for it.
4. Chat content often contains other people's personal information. Before sending it to a third party you must make sure you hold the necessary authorization and accept all responsibility arising from it.
5. Fees, quotas and risks of using a provider are between you and that provider.

13. Scope of network use
Other than the items above and web pages opened by the system browser when you tap a link, WeDeep makes no other network connections. Builds without a service address, for example one you build from source, do not connect to the WeDeep service and have no disabling rules, notices, update checks or usage statistics.

14. Permissions and system components
The permissions WeDeep requests are used only for its features: network access for the items above, and notifications for progress of tasks such as export. Root access is used only after you grant it, to read or write WeChat's data directory. For the import channel, WeDeep reads only the files you select.

15. Third-party components and intellectual property
1. Copyright in the software, interface and documentation of WeDeep belongs to the developer and the respective rights holders. You receive a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable and revocable license to use it.
2. Third-party open-source components included in WeDeep are governed by their own licenses, which prevail where they do not conflict with this agreement.
3. Rights in other people's messages, images, voice messages and files in your exports remain with their original owners. WeDeep claims none.
